root_cause.text: In the bq256xx charger driver probe path, `devm_request_threaded_irq()` was called before `bq256xx_power_supply_init()`, so the IRQ handler could run while `bq->charger` was still uninitialized during probe or after it had been freed during devm teardown, causing `power_supply_changed()` to use an invalid power_supply pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `bq256xx_power_supply_init(bq, &psy_cfg, dev)` above `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that requesting the IRQ first causes reverse-order devm cleanup to free/unregister the `power_supply` before the IRQ handler is removed, allowing `power_supply_changed()` to be called with a freed or uninitialized handle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize and register the bq256xx power supply during probe and abort probing if registration fails.
intent_record.what: A call to bq256xx_power_supply_init(bq, &psy_cfg, dev) was added in bq256xx_probe() before the IRQ setup, along with error handling that logs "Failed to register power supply" and returns the error code if initialization fails.
intent_record.how: At probe time, the driver now explicitly initializes and registers its power supply interface before requesting the IRQ. If that registration fails, probing stops immediately instead of continuing with a partially initialized device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move power supply registration out of the pre-hardware-init probe path to avoid premature registration failures and ensure chip initialization happens first.
intent_record.what: The call to bq256xx_power_supply_init(bq, &psy_cfg, dev) and its associated error handling block were removed from this location in bq256xx_probe(), deleting the registration attempt and early return on failure before the subsequent call to bq256xx_hw_init(bq).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe path no longer tries to register the power supply at this point before hardware initialization. This prevents probe failure caused by power supply registration occurring too early in the sequence and allows hardware initialization to proceed first.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by the IRQ handler being able to run before `bq->charger` is initialized. This change initializes/registers the bq256xx power supply during probe and fails probe if that setup does not succeed, directly addressing the uninitialized `bq->charger` aspect of the root cause.

The root cause is IRQ registration occurring before power-supply initialization, creating a race where the handler uses an uninitialized or freed charger pointer. This change instead reorders power-supply registration relative to hardware initialization to avoid premature registration failures, and does not directly address the IRQ-before-power-supply race or teardown issue.

candidates.rationale: This call requests and enables the IRQ before the power supply is initialized and registered, allowing the threaded IRQ handler to run while bq->charger is still uninitialized or later already freed during devm teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement requests and enables the IRQ before the probe path initializes and registers bq->charger via bq256xx_power_supply_init(). As a result, the threaded IRQ handler can run when bq->charger is still uninitialized during probe, or after teardown when the power_supply has already been freed, leading to power_supply_changed() using an invalid pointer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full probe path, IRQ registration, power-supply initialization, and the IRQ/work handlers that dereference `bq->charger`. The vulnerable ordering is present in `bq256xx_probe()`: `devm_request_threaded_irq(...)` is called inside `if (client->irq) { ... }` before `ret = bq256xx_power_supply_init(bq, &psy_cfg, dev);`. At the same time, both `bq256xx_irq_handler_thread()` and `bq256xx_usb_work()` call `power_supply_changed(bq->charger);` without checking whether `bq->charger` is initialized or still valid. Specifically, `bq256xx_irq_handler_thread()` ends with `power_supply_changed(bq->charger);`, and `bq256xx_usb_work()` does the same in the `USB_EVENT_NONE` case. Since `bq->charger` is only assigned in `bq256xx_power_supply_init()` via `bq->charger = devm_power_supply_register(...)`, an IRQ can run after IRQ registration but before that assignment, matching the root cause. There is no fix present such as moving IRQ registration after power-supply registration, disabling/synchronizing IRQ/work until initialization is complete, or guarding the handler against an uninitialized/freed `bq->charger`.
